name: Meeting the Orcs
summary: Meeting the Orcs is an audience in Orgrimmar arranged by Lady Sylvanas Windrunner to advance Silvermoon's petition to join the Horde. Carrying a personally endorsed letter from the Banshee Queen, an envoy travels from the Undercity across the sea to present the sin'dorei cause directly to the leadership in Durotar. It represents a pivotal diplomatic step in forging a formal pact between Quel'Thalas and the wider Horde.

sections.title: A Queen's Endorsement
sections.body: Even in undeath, Lady Sylvanas Windrunner retains a fierce protective bond with her former homeland of Quel'Thalas. Championing the blood elves' admission into the Horde, she personally endorses their diplomatic outreach to overcome the hesitation of the other member races. By sending an emissary from Silvermoon with a letter bearing her own seal, the Dark Lady aims to force the Orcish leadership to take the sin'dorei plea seriously.

sections.title: Crossing to Kalimdor
sections.body: The diplomatic mission requires leaving the gloomy vaults of the Undercity and taking a zeppelin across the Great Sea to the sun-baked canyons of Durotar. Presenting credentials to the warlords in Orgrimmar is not a mere formality: the orcs are culturally and geographically distant from the Quel'Thalas plight, harboring deep skepticism regarding the magical practices and historical loyalties of the high elves who once opposed them.

sections.title: Skepticism in the Valley of Strength
sections.body: Upon arrival in Orgrimmar, the bearer of the sealed letter finds a leadership guarded against easy alliances. While acknowledging Sylvanas's tenacity in lobbying for her kin, the orcish command remains cautious. Reading the Dark Lady's missive, the leadership questions whether the appearance of a single elven champion is truly enough to shift the strategic calculations of the entire Horde.

faq.q: Why is Sylvanas helping the blood elves join the Horde?
faq.answer: Sylvanas Windrunner was the Ranger-General of Silvermoon in life and fell defending her people from the Scourge. Despite her undeath and transformation into the Banshee Queen, she still cares for Quel'Thalas and has fought fiercely to give Silvermoon a seat at the Horde's negotiating table alongside Undercity and Orgrimmar.

faq.q: Where does this diplomatic journey lead?
faq.answer: The mission begins in the Royal Quarter of the Undercity and leads northwest to the zeppelin tower outside the ruins of Lordaeron. From there, the zeppelin carries travelers across the sea directly to Durotar, landing outside the gates of Orgrimmar.

faq.q: Why are the orcs hesitant to accept the blood elves?
faq.answer: The orcs fought the high elves in the Second War and know little of their recent rebirth as the sin'dorei. Orcish culture prizes physical martial prowess and honor, making them cautious of distant, magic-reliant kingdoms whose loyalties and struggles are unfamiliar to the clans in Kalimdor.

faq.q: What is inside the letter carried to Orgrimmar?
faq.answer: The missive contains Lady Sylvanas Windrunner's formal and personal endorsement of Silvermoon's pledge. It outlines the sin'dorei petition for membership in the Horde, backed by the Dark Lady's insistence that Quel'Thalas would be a valuable strategic partner.

faq.q: Who receives the diplomatic letter in Orgrimmar?
aliases: who do i turn this in to
faq.answer: The letter is brought before the highest leadership of the orcs residing in the Valley of Strength in Orgrimmar, where the letter's merits and Sylvanas's persistent lobbying are judged by the clan leaders.

faq.q: What follows after delivering the letter?
faq.answer: Delivering the endorsement leads directly to the question of formal allegiance, requiring the leadership in Orgrimmar to determine whether to accept Silvermoon's pledge and grant the sin'dorei full standing within the Horde.

angles.text: This embassy marks a critical expansion of the Horde's influence into the Eastern Kingdoms, bridging the gap between the Kalimdor clans and the ancient kingdom of Quel'Thalas.
For the Forsaken, bringing Silvermoon into the fold secures a vital northern ally on their border, easing their isolation amidst the hostile Scourge and Scarlet Crusade.
Orcs view the petition through the lens of honor and strength, skeptical of whether the arcane-reliant elves can pull their weight alongside the warriors of Durotar.
